---
title: "Trade and Supply Chain: who supplies the United States"
subtitle: "Each economy's share of US goods imports, by product chapter, and how it has moved since 2017"
---

```{python}
import pandas as pd
import plotly.express as px
from IPython.display import Markdown
from itables import init_notebook_mode, show

from pdi import site

init_notebook_mode(connected=False)

partners, meta = site.load("trade", "partners")
history, history_meta = site.load("trade", "share_history")
china, china_meta = site.load("trade", "china_shift")
chapters, chapters_meta = site.load("trade", "chapter_shifts")
check, check_meta = site.load("trade", "totals_check")
finding = meta.get("finding")
```

When a buyer changes supplier, it shows up first in the buyer's customs records. This page
reads the United States' records: what share of each kind of product it buys from China and
from six Southeast Asian economies, and how those shares have changed since 2017, the last
year before the first US tariffs on Chinese goods. It shows where the shares moved. It does
not show why.

## Share of all US goods imports

```{python}
#| output: asis
if partners.empty:
    print(site.empty_state(meta, "Import shares"))
else:
    print(site.finding_line(finding))
    month = pd.Timestamp(meta["latest_month"] + "-01").strftime("%B %Y")
    print(f'Twelve months to {month}, against the calendar year {meta["base_year"]}.\n')
    for _, r in partners.iterrows():
        way = "up" if r["shift_since_base"] >= 0 else "down"
        print(f'- {site.finding_badge(finding)} {r["name"]}: {r["share_pct"]:.1f}% of US goods '
              f'imports, {way} {abs(r["shift_since_base"]):.1f} points from '
              f'{r["share_base"]:.1f}% in {meta["base_year"]}.')
```

```{python}
if not history.empty:
    h = history.assign(period=pd.to_datetime(history["period"]))
    fig = px.line(h, x="period", y="share_pct", color="name", log_y=True,
                  labels={"share_pct": "Share of US goods imports, % (log scale)",
                          "period": "", "name": ""})
    fig.update_layout(height=420, margin=dict(l=10, r=10, t=10, b=10))
    fig.show()
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
if not history.empty:
    print(site.finding_line(finding))
```

## Where China's share fell, and who gained

One row per product chapter the United States imports at least
\$5 billion of a year. The first column is the change in China's share since 2017, in
percentage points; the others are the change for each Southeast Asian economy. A gain beside a
loss is a coincidence in timing until something else shows the goods are the same.

```{python}
if china.empty:
    display(Markdown(site.empty_state(china_meta, "China and Southeast Asia")))
else:
    t = china.assign(world_12m=china["world_12m"] / 1e9)[
        ["chapter", "name", "world_12m", "CN", "ID", "MY", "PH", "SG", "TH", "VN", "sea_total"]
    ].rename(columns={"chapter": "Chapter", "name": "Product", "world_12m": "US imports, $bn",
                      "CN": "China", "ID": "Indonesia", "MY": "Malaysia", "PH": "Philippines",
                      "SG": "Singapore", "TH": "Thailand", "VN": "Vietnam",
                      "sea_total": "Six together"}).round(1)
    show(t, paging=True, pageLength=25, showIndex=False, classes="display compact")
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
if not china.empty:
    print(site.finding_line(finding))
```

## Every partner and chapter

```{python}
if not chapters.empty:
    t = chapters.assign(usd_12m=chapters["usd_12m"] / 1e9)[
        ["name", "chapter", "chapter_name", "usd_12m", "share_pct", "share_base",
         "shift_since_base", "shift_on_year"]
    ].rename(columns={"name": "Partner", "chapter": "Chapter", "chapter_name": "Product",
                      "usd_12m": "Imports, $bn", "share_pct": "Share, %",
                      "share_base": f'Share in {meta["base_year"]}, %',
                      "shift_since_base": f'Change since {meta["base_year"]}, points',
                      "shift_on_year": "Change on a year earlier, points"}).round(2)
    show(t, paging=True, pageLength=25, showIndex=False, classes="display compact")
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
if not chapters.empty:
    print(site.finding_line(finding))
```

## Do these figures match what Census publishes?

```{python}
#| output: asis
if check.empty:
    print(site.empty_state(check_meta, "Totals check"))
else:
    ok = check_meta["criterion_met"]
    print(f'::: {{.verdict}}\n**{"Yes." if ok else "No."}** Across '
          f'{check_meta["partner_months"]:,} partner-months, the chapters on this page add up '
          f'to the all-commodity total Census publishes to within '
          f'{check_meta["worst_month_gap_pct"]:.4f}% at worst. The limit set in advance is '
          f'{check_meta["tolerance_pct"]:.0f}%, and a run that misses it stores nothing.\n:::\n')
    print(site.finding_line(check_meta.get("finding")))
```

```{python}
if not check.empty:
    last = check[check["year"] >= check["year"].max() - 1]
    t = last.assign(chapters_sum=last["chapters_sum"] / 1e9,
                    published_total=last["published_total"] / 1e9)[
        ["name", "year", "months", "chapters_sum", "published_total", "gap_pct"]
    ].rename(columns={"name": "Partner", "year": "Year", "months": "Months",
                      "chapters_sum": "Sum of chapters, $bn",
                      "published_total": "Published total, $bn", "gap_pct": "Gap, %"}).round(4)
    show(t, paging=False, showIndex=False, classes="display compact")
```
